newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-GERMANS THREATEN AS WIBERG GOES OUT.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-GERMANS THREATEN AS WIBERG GOES OUT.

text.p: Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg, the world and Olympic combined champion, stumbled out of the event at the Alpine skiing world championships on Thursday and left Germany well placed to win.

Italy's Morena Gallizio, fourth in the 1994 Olympic combined, led the field after the two legs of the slalom on a cold and gusty night in a total one minute 25.92 seconds. Switzerland's Marlies Oester was second, in 1:26.89.

But both women are slalom specialists and the real candidates to take the gold after the downhill, postponed to Friday morning after high winds on the Kandahar piste, were lurking just within striking distance.

Germany's Hilde Gerg, who won a World Cup super-G in Val d'Isere in December and also finished second in a downhill in January and in a combined this month, emerged third fastest on the floodlit piste 2.30 seconds behind Gallizio.
Right behind, just 0.05 seconds slower, was her compatriot and Olympic downhill champion Katja Seizinger while little-known Swiss Catherine Borghi was 0.01 behind Seizinger.
They now have a very difficult but not totally impossible task since Oester has not raced a downhill this year while Gallizio admitted that she would need a perfect run.
Much will depend on whether the downhill starts from the regular point or from the lower super-G start, which will allow racers less distance and less chance to make up time.
The downhill that was called off in the morning had been lowered to the super-G start but even that was too windy, with dangerous gusts of up to 75 kph in some spots.
"It would be hard to make up the distance on such a short course," said Gerg. But with a little bit of luck and if I attack, then maybe I can do it."

Seizinger, a top hope for Saturday's main downhill, said the conditions were demanding with the wind blowing loose snow around the hill and buffeting the few spectators, but she was still optimistic about her medal chances.
"I didn't want to ski out. Maybe I was too cautious on the upper part," the German said.
Wiberg, who has won a gold medal at every world championships or Olympic Games that she has competed in, paid the price for too little caution.
She hooked a gate with her left ski on the first run of the slalom and was left facing the real prospect of leaving Sestriere without a medal after two golds last year.
Saturday's regular downhill, assuming it goes ahead and is not disrupted by bad weather, too, is her last hope.
"I haven't been very lucky in these world championships but I have been very lucky in the World Cup," said the overall World Cup leader, who has been fighting a cold here.

"I will try to laugh about it," said Wiberg of her misfortune. She confirmed that she would compete in Saturday's downhill but did not rate her chances very highly in a discipline that she has never before won.
"Seizinger, (Swiss Heidi) Zurbriggen and (Italy's Isolde) Kostner were all very good in training."
She said her goal now was to win the overall World Cup to go to the 1998 Nagano Olympics as the champion.
Austria's Anita Wachter, the silver medallist last year, and Norway's Marianne Kjoerstad, who took bronze, had a slim chance of medals after finishing eighth and 11th.
Wachter was 3.72 seconds off the pace.
Only 19 women will take part in the combined downhill, after four of the 23 starters went out of the slalom.
